name: Nissan 370Z
reliability: 7/10 — strong VQ engine, but the clutch slave cylinder failure is a real black mark
popular_mods: Intake, high-flow cats / test pipes, catback exhaust
Uprev or Ecutek ECU tune (modest NA gains)
Forced induction (turbo/supercharger kits) for serious power
Coilovers, sway bars, big brake kit

generations.350Z (Z33, 2003–2008): Predecessor. 3.5L VQ35 V6 (287–306hp). The car that revived the Z nameplate in the US.
generations.370Z (Z34, 2009–2020): 3.7L VQ37VHR, 332hp. World's first manual with SynchroRev Match. Long 12-year run with minimal changes. Nismo trim made 350hp.
generations.Nissan Z (RZ34, 2023–present): Successor. 3.0L twin-turbo VR30DDTT, 400hp (shared with Q50 Red Sport). Dropped the displacement-based name.

common_issues: Concentric slave cylinder (CSC) failure — cheap plastic part, requires transmission removal ($1,500-$3,500)
Oil consumption (shared VQ trait) at higher mileage
Rear tire wear from aggressive factory camber
maintenance_tips: Replace the plastic CSC with an aftermarket metal unit proactively
Use Nissan ester oil and check level regularly
Get an alignment to slow rear tire wear
Let the gearbox warm up before hard 2nd-gear shifts

engine.detail: 3.7L VQ37VHR V6 with VVEL variable valve lift - 332 hp and 270 lb-ft, a rev-happy naturally aspirated unit.
engine.watch: Prone to high oil temps under track or hard use that trigger a limp mode near 280F, so an oil cooler is wise; some cars also drink oil at higher miles.

drivetrain.detail: RWD with a 6-speed manual (the world's first with SynchroRev Match rev-matching) or a 7-speed automatic.
drivetrain.watch: The plastic concentric slave cylinder can fail and needs the transmission dropped to replace - swap in a metal unit; 2nd-gear synchro also feels notchy when cold.

suspension.detail: Struts up front and a multilink rear on a rigid Z34 chassis, tuned firm for a short-wheelbase sports coupe.
suspension.watch: Aggressive factory rear camber chews the inner edges off the rear tires fast - get a proper alignment to slow the wear.

brakes.detail: Sport trim adds 4-piston front / 2-piston rear Akebono calipers on 14-inch rotors; base cars get smaller single-piston brakes.
brakes.watch: The Akebono setup is known for brake judder - Nissan issued a TSB - as pads and rotors can warp or build up material and vibrate under highway braking.
